scope: Emitter spike for effect rows (roadmap S4.1 term 1). Adjudicates G-CODEGEN and the S7.5 ramp (R1/R2/R3) over the artifacts frozen by design-doc S12.1. The prototype it measures is THROWAWAY: it is not the E2 implementation and must not be merged as one.

A1.what: tools/calor-allowlist-audit/allowlist-audit.calr, the dogfood utility built in CI at .github/workflows/test.yml:174. 127 lines, no higher-order code.
A1.note: before and after are byte-identical sources: A1 has no function-typed position, so there is no row to add. It is the regression module.

A2.what: bench/corpus/MediatR/src/MediatR/Pipeline/RequestPreProcessorBehavior.cs at the pinned SHA fb309026775ef953a64fb5339d074426c1ad2c37 (29 lines by `grep -c ''`), converted to Calor by `calor convert`.
deviations: The file's three MediatR dependencies (RequestHandlerDelegate, IPipelineBehavior, IRequestPreProcessor) are inlined into before/A2.source.cs before conversion, because `calor convert` validates the round-tripped C# and fails with four CS0246 errors on the file alone. The class body is the corpus file's, verbatim.
async is modelled as a sync-shaped row over a Task-returning function, exactly as design-doc S11 says the spike should.

A3.what: The four combinator fixtures of S7.4, in their AFTER forms.
deviations: A3-map: the type parameters <T, U> of S7.4's form are dropped and the fixture is monomorphic in TYPES ([i32] / Func<i32,i32>), keeping only `eff e`. Reason: `SARR{T} n` emits `new int[n]` for a type-parameter element type and the generated C# fails with CS0029 — a pre-existing codegen gap unrelated to rows, and generic TYPE parameters are deferred by calor-direction.md:33 anyway. The effect-polymorphic content of the fixture is unchanged.
A3-map: S7.4's body uses `SIX{out i} = ...`, which is not a live section marker (`Calor0006: Unknown section marker`). Transcribed to `SSETIDX{out} i ...`, the real spelling.

A3-match: S7.4's `?T:opt` / `is_some` / `unwrap` Option surface does not compile (`Calor0106: Unknown operator 'is-some'`), so the option is modelled as a (bool, value) pair. The row content — ONE variable across BOTH arms, so `e` is their join — is exactly S7.4's.

A3-middleware: the member-level spelling is used, per the A3 spelling decision below. after/A3-middleware.calr is the CORRECTED program (R1's clean case); after/A3-middleware-broadening.calr is S7.4's `{e, cw}`-against-`{e}` spelling (R2's rejection case); after/A3-middleware-alpha.calr renames the implementation's variable to `f` (the alpha-equivalence proof).

consequences: S7.3's last table row STANDS as written: class/interface-level `eff` stays FORBIDDEN in E2.
S9's seventh parser insertion point stays CONDITIONAL and is scheduled at ZERO cost: position 1 is already permitted and needed no new insertion point.
P18's seventh rejection case stays `Rejected_ClassOrInterfaceLevel`; it does not flip to `_Permitted`.
evidence: after/A3-middleware.calr compiles clean: the interface member binds `eff e`, the implementing class member binds `eff e`, and the implementation is accepted.
after/A3-middleware-broadening.calr is rejected with Calor0421 naming `[cw]` against an interface row of `[pure]` — the ordinary shared relation, no rank-1 branch.

after/A3-middleware-alpha.calr binds `eff e` on the INTERFACE and `eff f` on the IMPLEMENTATION and still compiles. This is the proof design-doc S12.1 says W1c did not supply: `fits` DOES identify the interface's variable with the implementation's, because a row carries BINDER INDICES, not names.
after/A2.calr and after/A2-broadening.calr reproduce both halves on the real MediatR shape.
a3MiddlewareSpelling.openResidual: The MediatR interface is someone else's (S14 Q1). Member-level `eff` means a Calor implementation can be effect-polymorphic without editing the interface ONLY IF the interface is also written in Calor with the `eff` binder. For a truly external C#-declared IPipelineBehavior there is no Calor row on the interface at all, so the implementation's row has nothing to be checked against and the site routes to the assumed/unknown channel. The spike does not close that; it shows the spelling works when both sides are Calor.

gCodegen.definition: Design-doc S12.2. For each artifact the before/ and after/ .calr are emitted by the SAME compiler and the .g.cs compared. `strict` is byte-for-byte; `moduloLineDirectives` additionally normalises the line NUMBER inside `#line N "<source>.calr"`, which tracks the source and necessarily moves when the author adds annotation lines.

A2.explanation: Every differing byte is inside a `#line` directive, and the two files are the same length. after/A2.calr has two more source lines than before/A2.calr (the SE{e} row on the interface member and on the implementation), so the directives that point INTO the source move by two. No emitted C# construct differs. The `eff` binder is fully erased: the emitted `Handle` signature is `Task<TResponse> Handle(TRequest, RequestHandlerDelegate<TResponse>, CancellationToken)` on both sides, with no `<e>`.

gCodegen.honestReading: Five of six artifacts are byte-identical under the STRICT reading, including all four A3 fixtures — because an inline row is written on the SAME line as the type it annotates, so adding one shifts nothing. A2 is the one artifact whose rows sit on their own added lines, and it is byte-identical everywhere except the source-position directives. The design's claim — rows are erased at codegen — holds. The feature-wide gate does NOT block.

R1.claim: Each of Map, Match, middleware/next and callbacks, in its AFTER form, compiles with zero Calor0424, zero Calor0425 and zero Calor0404, without --permissive-effects and without any SCSHARP block.
R1.evidence: after/A3-map.diagnostics.txt, after/A3-match.diagnostics.txt, after/A3-middleware.diagnostics.txt, after/A3-callback.diagnostics.txt — all four report `exit: 0` and `diagnostics: 0` on a PLAIN compile.
R1.beforeContrast: Each before/ counterpart is rejected today with Calor0418 at the invocation (2 occurrences for A3-middleware, 1 each for the others).
R1.caveat: R1's bar is the ABSENCE of three codes. The prototype is deliberately additive — every new code path is gated on a row being PRESENT — so the Calor0425-on-omitted-row path of S3.5 is NOT implemented, and a row-less function-typed position still reaches today's Calor0418 rather than 0425. R1 is therefore weaker evidence than its wording suggests: it says the four combinators type-check cleanly, not that every 0425 route was exercised. Stated here rather than left for a reader to discover.

R2.claim: In the MediatR shape, an implementation row {e, cw} against an interface row {e} is rejected by the ORDINARY fits relation as Calor0421, and the corrected program is accepted by it, with no rank-1-specific branch in CheckEffectVariance.
evidence: CheckEffectVariance's two IsSubsetOf calls were replaced by two calls to the SHARED EffectRow.Fits. There is no `if (row.IsPolymorphic)` branch anywhere in CheckEffectVariance — the alpha-equivalence lives inside Fits, which sites 2 and 6 also call.
after/A2.diagnostics.txt: the corrected program raises no variance diagnostic.
after/A3-middleware-alpha.calr compiles with DIFFERENT variable names on the two sides.
R2.residual: The interface must itself be Calor for the row to exist on it. See a3MiddlewareSpelling.openResidual and design-doc S14 Q1.

R3.claim: Instantiation is decidable by S7.4's one-line solve on all four fixtures, with no case needing a second variable, a constraint set, or a fixpoint.
evidence: The solve is a single forward pass over the argument list inside CheckRowedArguments: `e := join { rho(arg_j) minus rho_decl_j : parameter j's row mentions e }`. No worklist, no iteration to a fixpoint, no second pass.
A3-map / A3-match instantiate `e` from METHOD-GROUP arguments (Double/Announce, Identity/Zero/Shout) — Match joins two arguments into ONE variable, which is the case S7.4 calls out.

A3-middleware instantiates VARIABLE-TO-VARIABLE: Handle passes its own rowed parameter `next` (row [#0]) to RunTwice's rowed parameter `g`. Narrowing Handle's own row to SE{} makes the fixture fail with `Calor0410: Function 'Handle' instantiates an effect variable of 'RunTwice' from an argument whose row mentions an effect variable this declaration does not declare.` — so the solve is load-bearing, not decorative.
A3-callback needs NO effect variable at all, exactly as S7.4 predicts.

ramp.verdictRule: VALIDATED iff R1 and R2 and R3

implemented: Calor0404 / Calor0405 / Calor0424 / Calor0425 allocated in Diagnostic.cs.

EffectRow + RowFit: the three-point lattice, the join, the nine-cell fits, ExtraEffects, ToDisplayString. Placed in the EXISTING Effects/EffectSet.cs, not S9's planned new Effects/EffectRow.cs, so the spike needs no Calor-first allowlist-precursor PR.
Row syntax at position 5 (inline parameter) and position 8 (field), under the line-adjacency rule, each with the Calor0405 parser-stage recovery.

The `eff` modifier in SF / SAF / SMT / SAMT type-parameter lists, with the one-token lookahead that keeps a type parameter literally named `eff` working (Z4), and S7.2(c)'s ban on naming a variable after a live effect code.
Effect variables recorded as BINDER INDICES, never names — the mechanism that makes site 5 alpha-equivalent.
Sites 2 (argument), 5 (interface implementation), 4 (override) and 6 (rank-1 instantiation), sites 4 and 5 by routing CheckEffectVariance through the shared EffectRow.Fits.
notImplemented: Positions 4 (SI tag parameter), 6 (return), 7 (SB binding) — the AFTER forms do not use them.

FunctionBoundType.Row / ParameterRows. The spike carries rows on the AST and reads them in the effect pass; it does NOT put them in the bound tree, because the effect pass is an AST walk (design doc S2) and the bound tree is not on the path. E2 still owes S8.2.
The Calor0425-on-omitted-row path (S3.5): a row-less function-typed position still reaches today's Calor0418. Deliberate — it is what keeps the prototype additive and every committed test green.
The Assumed row is defined in the lattice but never CONSTRUCTED: nothing maps EffectResolutionStatus or the assumption side-table into it (S8.4, P21).
S4.1's Subtypes widening, S4.5's removal of the Calor0420/0421 permissive demotion, the CalorEmitter round-trip for rows (P4), and eng/ast-schema.json's four Row children.
prototype.mustNotBeMergedAsIs: All of it. The prototype answers the ramp; it is not an implementation. In particular the parser-level effect-variable scope (a single mutable list on Parser, reset by every type-parameter list) is a spike shortcut that E2 must replace with a proper scope carried through binding.
